chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who pledged a pledge for an indefinite time, then the pledgor was absent, is there a time for which his pledge is sold? He said, 'No, until he comes.'

key_terms.إِلَى غَيْرِ وَقْتٍ: For an indefinite time / without a fixed deadline

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a pledge if the borrower is absent and the pledge period was indefinite?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that in a pledge for an indefinite period, the creditor cannot unilaterally sell the collateral upon the debtor's absence; the debtor's return is required to finalize the transaction. This ruling underscores the principle of protecting the debtor's rights against arbitrary disposal of their property, a key concern in Shia jurisprudence regarding commercial contracts. It highlights the necessity of mutual consent or the debtor's presence to convert the pledge into a sale, ensuring fairness in debt settlement.
